Source: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1457

## Problem (2026.10.13, also 2026.10.10)
When `pm list` output is truncated by the default output token budget, the response carries `next_cursor`, but that cursor is an **output cursor** (`continuation_kind: "output_cursor"`). An agent following the help text cannot use it:
- `pm list --help` documents `--after <cursor>` as "Continue after an opaque next_cursor from a previous list response".
- `pm list --help` does **not** list `--output-cursor` at all.
- `pm list … --after <that next_cursor>` refuses with `invalid_query_cursor` / "Query cursor version or payload is unsupported". The refusal has no recovery hint and never mentions `--output-cursor`, even though the same cursor works with `--output-cursor`.

The only pointer is buried in `output_budget_truncation.recovery.cli = "--output-cursor"`.

## Reproduction (synthetic, about 1 minute)
```sh
T=$(mktemp -d) && cd "$T" && git init -q && export PM_PATH=$T/.agents/pm PM_AUTHOR=repro
pm init --prefix cr
for i in $(seq 1 120); do pm create --type Task --title "Synthetic continuation item number $i with a deliberately long title" --description "$(printf 'padding %.0s' $(seq 1 40))"; done
c=$(pm --json list --status all --limit 500 | jq -r .next_cursor)   # applied_limit 33, truncated, continuation_kind output_cursor
pm --json list --status all --limit 500 --after "$c"               # invalid_query_cursor, no recovery command
pm --json list --status all --limit 500 --output-cursor "$c"       # works (next 33 rows)
```

## Real-world impact
A script mirroring 266 knowledge items wrote the documented loop (`--limit 500`, then follow `next_cursor` with `--after`). It failed on the second page. An earlier version that took `.items` without checking `truncated` would silently have seen only the first 129 of 266 rows (the budget cut `--limit 500` down to 129), and would have created duplicates on re-runs.

## Proposal
1. `--after` should accept an output cursor for the same query fingerprint and continue transparently, since both are opaque continuation tokens for the same query. If they must stay distinct, refuse with a recovery command that substitutes `--output-cursor <cursor>`.
2. List `--output-cursor` in `pm list --help` (and in search/context help), and make the `--after` help say which `continuation_kind` it accepts.
3. Consider naming the field after the flag that consumes it: keep `next_cursor` for query cursors and use `next_output_cursor` for budget continuations, or document that `continuation_kind` decides the flag.

Related closed work: #1371 (budget continuation across producer cursors).
